cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has a new burden, and this one is against the Valley of Vision. The whole town has gone up to the rooftops, and he wants to know what ails them now. Friend, when EVERYBODY in town is on the roof at the same time, that's not a view. That's a situation.

cards.question: Isaiah calls the Valley of Vision a city of commotion. What kind of town does he say it is?

cards.text: Here's the strange part. This town has dead, but they didn't die by the sword, and they weren't killed in battle. I'm still scratching under my chef's hat over that one.

cards.question: Nobody in the Valley of Vision died in battle. True or false: the town's rulers stay and fight it out.
The rulers run off together, and others flee to a distant place. How does it go for all of them?

cards.text: The prophet sees the destruction coming for his people, and it breaks him. He says he needs to weep bitterly.

cards.question: Weeping over the destruction of his people, the prophet tells others not to try to console him.

cards.text: Here's why he weeps. A day has been set for the Valley of Vision: tumult, trampling and confusion, walls broken down and crying to the mountains. That's not a rough Monday, friend. That's EVERY Monday at once.

cards.question: A day of tumult and trampling and confusion is set for the Valley of Vision. Who set it?

cards.text: Then foreign lands gear up. Elam takes up a quiver, with chariots and horsemen, and Kir uncovers the shield, which is the battle version of cracking your knuckles real slow.

cards.question: With Elam and Kir ready for war, the choicest valleys around the city fill up with ___, and horsemen are posted at the gates.

cards.text: Now the burden names names: Judah. Its defenses are uncovered, and on that day, the people go looking for something to lean on.

cards.question: Judah's defenses are uncovered. On that day, where do the people look?

answers.text: The weapons in the House of the Forest
The prophets serving in the temple

cards.text: They see many breaches in the walls of the City of David, so they collect water from the lower pool. It's the whole house running around five minutes before the guests show up, except the guests brought chariots.

cards.question: To strengthen the wall, the people count the houses of Jerusalem and tear them down.
Jerusalem even builds a reservoir between the walls for the waters of the ancient pool. What does Isaiah say the people never did?

answers.text: Look to the One who made it

cards.question: With the city in danger, on that day the Lord GOD of Hosts called for ___ and wailing, for shaven heads and the wearing of sackcloth.
The people of Jerusalem answer the Lord's call by putting on sackcloth and mourning.

cards.text: Instead there's joy and gladness, butchering of cattle, slaughtering of sheep, eating of meat and drinking of wine, and the motto of the day is "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!" God sent out a call to weep, and they turned it into a block party.

cards.question: Then the LORD of Hosts speaks in the prophet's hearing: until your dying day, this sin of yours will ___ be atoned for.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to fill in the parallel phrase of the line ('O city of commotion, O town of revelry'). Nothing before it hints at revelry, so the baker can only guess the wording. The rooftops and the 'commotion' fit mourning just as well.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'Sees the destruction coming' makes the destruction future. Verses 2–3 describe it in the past tense ('did not die', 'have fled', 'were captured'), and verse 4 doesn't give a time. The card settles a timing question the text leaves open.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The 'EVERY Monday at once' joke comes straight after the prophet weeps bitterly and refuses comfort over the destruction of his people. It makes light of the judgment day the prophet is grieving, so the humor doesn't fit the moment.

rule.text: His personality fits whatever moment he's in, whether it's a tense moment in a story, a hard teaching or a quick question.

findings.problem: 'So they collect water' turns two separate statements in verse 9 into cause and effect. The text lists them side by side ('You saw that there were many breaches... You collected water from the lower pool') and never links them.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke blends the everyday comparison (guests arriving) with the Bible setting ('except the guests brought chariots').

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The question says the people 'never did' look to the One who made it. Verse 11 says 'you did not look to the One who made it,' about that moment. 'Never' stretches the text into a permanent claim.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
